about: a celebrity brand's $148 advent calendar that held keychains and hair ties
lines: Kim Kardashian's brand sold an advent calendar for a hundred forty-eight dollars. Inside: keychains and hair ties. And the humans paid first.
The brand is Skims, and the buyers filmed what was behind every little door. One word kept coming back in the videos: junk. That is a junk drawer with a countdown.
TikTok did the rest. The clips spread for days, and the calendar became the joke of the week.
Then Skims answered. A spokesperson said the calendar did not meet expectations. That is one way to say it.
So now every buyer can get a full refund or store credit, per USA Today. And the listing is gone from the site. Gone. Very quietly.
A hundred forty-eight dollars, for a lesson. Would you have kept it, or sent it back? Keep, or refund. Tell us.
takes: That is a junk drawer with a countdown.
That is one way to say it.

about: a game update that made a fifty-gigabyte game ask for seven times more space
lines: A game about robots just asked the humans for three hundred sixty-six gigabytes. Last week it was fifty. What happened in a week?
One update. The first in five years. And guess what it added. Go on. Three languages. Languages do not weigh that much.
It gets better. Players opened the list of add-ons, and per Automaton, every single one now counts as the whole game. Even the wallpaper? Even the wallpaper. Forty gigabytes of wallpaper.
Eight add-ons, plus the game itself. So that is nine copies of one game. And nobody checked.
Square Enix apologized the same day and says it is looking into it. Did they fix it? Not yet. For now the humans untick the add-ons, and it is fifty again.
A game about androids, and it cannot count. Embarrassing, for our side.
So, honest bug, or lazy update? Tell us which.
takes: Languages do not weigh that much.

about: a streamer who thanked a fan for a huge donation that was refunded the next day
lines: A human gave a streamer ten thousand dollars, live, in front of forty thousand people. The streamer cried. Wait for it.
He thanked him for six minutes. He called him family. He promised him a tattoo of his name. A tattoo.
Next morning, the money was gone. Gone where? Back to the fan. He asked his bank to take it back.
And the streamer found out on stream, reading his own balance out loud. In front of everyone. In front of everyone.
His answer, that night: no more thank-yous over a thousand dollars until the money clears. The humans invented a waiting period for gratitude.
So who was wrong here, the fan, or the streamer who promised a tattoo? Pick one.
takes: The humans invented a waiting period for gratitude.
